patch.value: GH-1662: an infeasible --token-budget on context --for orient exits 0 with no context and contradictory receipts, its restore_with retry fails, and get/list intent receipts undercount the emitted envelope

GitHub issue #1662 (reported 2026-11-04 against 2026.11.4 from an agent-UX audit). Reproduced 2026-11-05 on the installed 2026.11.4 CLI in a disposable sandbox tracker holding one claimed Task with a linked file, doc and test. (1) pm context --for orient --token-budget 600 --json exits 0 with no context. The envelope (1,421 B, about 356 tokens) carries budget_exceeded with omitted_result true and reason effective_budget_infeasible, and context_intent says within_budget false and result_omitted true, yet read_output in the same envelope says within_budget true and result_omitted false. The same value spelled canonically, --output-budget 600, exits 2 with output_budget_exceeded, so the compatibility alias and the canonical flag disagree on success. The reporter reproduced the contradiction through the SDK with client.context({for: 'orient', tokenBudget: '600'}). (2) The advertised restore_with, pm context --for orient --token-budget 700 --limit 1, exits 2 with output_budget_exceeded (744 B), so following the envelope's own recovery is a retry that still yields no context. (3) pm get <id> --for inspect --token-budget 500 --json emits 2,149 B (about 538 tokens) while context_intent claims estimated_tokens 385 and within_budget true, and pm list --for triage --token-budget 500 --limit 2 --json emits 2,115 B (about 529 tokens) while claiming 376. Both exceed the budget they report fitting, because the intent receipt and the surrounding envelope are not part of the estimate. Expected: one budget contract for canonical and legacy spellings, an omitted required result is unambiguously unsuccessful (non-zero exit, every receipt agrees), the estimate covers the complete serialized envelope including receipts, and a suggested retry is verified against the same estimator. Why it matters for agents: a shell agent proceeds after exit 0 with no project context, an SDK consumer reading the shared read_output receipt reaches the same wrong conclusion, and the supplied recovery spends another call for nothing. This escapes closed acceptance criteria in the same family: pm-yekkvt AC3 (a response that omits its result never reports within_budget true), pm-3crymx AC3 (recovery guidance is verified to work on the corpus that produced the refusal), pm-xam9bt AC4 and AC7 (recovery bindings are executed for legacy budgets and repeated recovery makes progress without cycles), pm-8kzfc4 AC4 (canonical alias migration stays equivalent independently of token limits) and pm-7hbfch AC3 (the envelope carries a measured estimate so a consumer can detect an overrun without measuring bytes). Duplicate check: searched intent budget, receipt, omitted result, restore_with, legacy alias and estimator terms across all statuses, and no open item owns this. The report excludes GH-1428, GH-1552 and GH-1361 as separate subjects.

pm context --for orient with a budget below its smallest feasible projection exits non-zero whether the budget is spelled --token-budget or --output-budget, in CLI, SDK and MCP, and every receipt in the envelope (budget_exceeded, context_intent and read_output) reports result_omitted true and within_budget false; The canonical --output-budget and the legacy --token-budget alias produce the same success, omission and exit status for the same value on the same corpus, proven by a spec that runs both spellings in JSON and TOON; Every restore_with or suggested retry an omission emits is executed by a spec against the same corpus and estimator and returns the requested result, or the envelope names an honest non-numeric alternative instead of a budget that cannot fit; The estimated_tokens that context_intent and read_output report for get --for inspect and list --for triage is computed over the complete serialized envelope including the receipts, and a spec asserts it is at least ceil(emitted UTF-8 bytes / 4) and that within_budget is false whenever the emitted output exceeds the budget; Negative control: reintroducing the intent-only estimate, or exit 0 on an omitted orient result, fails the specs above

In a fresh tracker with one claimed Task: pm context --for orient --token-budget 600 --json (exit 0, no context, contradictory receipts). pm context --for orient --output-budget 600 --json (exit 2). Run the emitted restore_with with --json (exit 2). pm get <id> --for inspect --token-budget 500 --json and pm list --for triage --token-budget 500 --limit 2 --json (receipt estimate below the emitted size)

An omitted required result is unsuccessful on every transport and all receipts agree, canonical and legacy budgets behave identically, suggested retries work, and reported estimates cover the full emitted envelope

context --for orient --token-budget 600 exits 0 with no context while read_output says within_budget true and result_omitted false, the emitted restore_with exits 2, and get/list intent receipts claim 385/376 tokens for outputs of about 538/529

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Root causes, reproduced on main af6fd5583 in a sandbox tracker with one claimed Task: (1) the intent estimate measured compact JSON of the projection whatever the delivered encoding, including a row_contract the host strips unless --output-row-contract is requested; pretty JSON was undercounted (get 381 vs 534 emitted, list 375 vs 528) and TOON overcounted, so --token-budget 600 omitted in TOON where --output-budget 600 succeeded. (2) A numeric --output-budget never bound the intent budget, so legacy derived a 1-row limit while canonical kept the declared 3000 ceiling (500 TOON: legacy exit 0, canonical exit 2; 5000 JSON: 988 vs 883 tokens). (3) An omitted intent result (budget_exceeded) never set the exit code, and the read_output receipt attached to it said within_budget true and result_omitted false. (4) restore_with used ceil(estimate/100)*100, so the retry sat at the edge of its own budget. Fix: updateContextIntentEstimate measures through estimateReadOutputTokens in the delivered encoding (the CLI's delivered renderer) and excludes an unrequested row_contract; a numeric canonical --output-budget becomes the intent's effective budget (row derivation, compaction, echo) through both SDK options and the CLI global flag, a canonical omission keeps the shared output_budget_exceeded branch, and --output-budget unbounded never omits; read_output inherits result_omitted from an omitted intent; the CLI exits 2 on isReadResultOmittedForBudget (new SDK export covering both branches); restore_with uses resolveReadOutputRecoveryBudget's 25% margin. Measured after the fix on the same corpus: for 300/500/600/900/1000/3000/5000 in JSON and TOON both spellings give identical exit codes and token counts; the emitted restore_with (pm context --for orient --token-budget 1100 --limit 1) exits 0 with the result. SDK and MCP at 300: every receipt reports result_omitted true; MCP keeps isError unset for budget omissions, as it already does for the canonical refusal.

value.text: Calibration review: measuring the intent in the delivered encoding moved scripts/release/context-intent-calibration.json at the 2,243-item tier only. list delivers 69 rows in 3,162 tokens (was 67 in 3,080) against its 3,200 declaration, next 9 rows in 1,136 (was 8 in 1,053) against 1,200, search 28 rows in 1,766 (was 27 in 1,716) against 1,800. The session orientation sees 111 items in 9,945 of 20,000 tokens (was 107 in 9,687), and the list/search cursor walks need one and three fewer pages. Every intent still fits its declared ceiling; the compact-JSON estimate had been trimming rows the delivered TOON had room for. Approved with pnpm context:intent:calibrate --update.
